content: The Student National Medical Association (SNMA) is the oldest and largest organization in the United States that specifically addresses the needs and concerns of medical students of color. Its membership includes over 6,000 individuals, comprising medical students, pre-medical students, residents, and physicians. The SNMA was established in 1964 by medical students from Howard University and Meharry Medical College. For over 40 years, it has been dedicated to serving both underserved communities and the needs of medical students. Local SNMA chapters, which are based at medical schools and some undergraduate institutions across the United States, organize and implement programs and activities tailored to their communities. The programs developed by SNMA are specifically designed to address the healthcare needs of underserved populations and communities of color. Furthermore, the organization is committed to ensuring that medical education and healthcare services are culturally sensitive and responsive to the needs of diverse populations. It also aims to increase the representation of African-American, Latino, and other students of color in medical schools, supporting them through both entry and completion of their medical education. The SNMA is dedicated to supporting underrepresented minority medical students, both current and future, while also addressing the healthcare disparities faced by underserved communities. It strives to increase the number of physicians who are not only clinically excellent but also culturally competent and socially conscious. There are over 130 SNMA chapters located at medical schools nationwide, and more than 70 undergraduate institutions host Minority Association of Pre-medical Students (MAPS) chapters. Both SNMA and MAPS chapters are officially recognized by the national SNMA organization through the annual submission of chapter renewal forms. Members of SNMA are categorized as either Active or Associate members, both of whom pay national membership dues. Membership in a local chapter is not a requirement for national membership. While SNMA chapters operate independently, they are required to adhere to the national Constitution and Bylaws, similar to the governance structure of SNMA regions.
